tasks.title: Calling dotenv.config() results in a TypeError
tasks.publicBody:
Since upgrading from dotenv 14.2.0 to 14.3.0 I get the following error when calling `dotenv.config()`

CODE (foo.js):
```
...
import * as dotenv from "dotenv";
dotenv.config(); // line 20
...
```

ERROR:
```
$ yarn build
$ tslint -c tslint.json -p tsconfig.json --fix
$ tsc
$ node --es-module-specifier-resolution=node .
file:///..../foo.js:20
dotenv.config();
       ^

TypeError: dotenv.config is not a function
    at file:///..../foo.js:20:8
    at ModuleJob.run (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:185:25)
    at async Promise.all (index 0)
    at async ESMLoader.import (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:281:24)
    at async loadESM (node:internal/process/esm_loader:88:5)
    at async handleMainPromise (node:internal/modules/run_main:65:12)
```

Downgrading to 14.2.0 solves the error.
tasks.contractNotes: Restore public namespace import config() and parse() while preserving CommonJS/default imports, actual custom-file loading, existing environment handling, and returned error behavior. Independent assertions are API-level, no requirement to emit exact upstream statements. Fix production change is only lib/main.js.

tasks.title: # inside double quotes still treated as inline comment
tasks.publicBody:
v14.2.0
`SOME_KEY={"field1":"some value", "field2": "stops here#this is discarded"}`
When above line is parsed generates the following output
`SOME_KEY: {"field1":"some value", "field2": "stops here`
which in turns gives a SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input
tasks.contractNotes: Retain complete unquoted JSON strings containing a non-whitespace-preceded hash, as original issue reproduction requires, plus retain documented basic parsing/comment/quote/trim/Buffer/newline behavior. No new multiline, interpolation, hash-with-whitespace-inside-unquoted-JSON requirements. The historical patch explicitly specifies whitespace before inline comments; broad parser overhaul is not demanded.

tasks.title: Memory leak when using abort signals
tasks.publicBody: We have encountered a memory leak issue. After an extensive search for the source of the leak, it was found that it occurred in pMap. Upon reviewing the source code of your package, I discovered that you subscribe to the AbortSignal event but do not unsubscribe from it, which causes the memory leak.
tasks.contractNotes: Settled mapping must not keep AbortSignal event listeners; verify success, empty and skipped input, mapper and aggregate errors, shared-signal reuse, and active cancellation while preserving results/error identity and optional-signal behavior. Uses Node public getEventListeners API rather than monkeypatching implementation. Pre-aborted cleanup is deliberately not graded because the historical reference still adds a listener after already-aborted rejection.

tasks.title: The parse method returns incorrect output when both strictNullHandling and allowEmptyArrays are set to true
tasks.contractNotes: Issue states stringify/parse round-trip with strictNullHandling and allowEmptyArrays must preserve empty arrays. Cases vary field names, nested paths, encoded brackets and preserve scalar-null and nonempty-array behavior. No solution comments enter actor prompt.

tasks.title: Parsing object with array doesn't split a value
tasks.contractNotes: Issue explicitly expects comma splitting of object-form query input, just as string input. Cases vary flat/nested keys and multiple fields while preserving no-comma, comma:false, primitive values, and input immutability.

tasks.title: Globstar not matching zero
tasks.publicBody:
According to the docs, minimatch should behave like Bash 4.1.

According to this comment, the `/path/**/*.html` pattern should match `/path/to/page.html`, `/path/to/web/page.html`, and also `/path/page.html`, for Bash 4 and above. This works in my Bash 4.4.20.

However, if I use minimatch to create a RegExp for the pattern above:

```
const makeRe = require("minimatch").makeRe;
const regex = makeRe("/path/**/*.html");
```
the resulting RegExp seems to be `^(?:\/path\/(?:(?!(?:\/|^)\.).)*?\/(?!\.)(?=.)[^\/]*?\.html)$`, which although matches `/path/to/page.html` and `/path/to/web/page.html`, it doesn't match `/path/page.html`

tasks.contractNotes: Issue requires makeRe globstar to span zero or more directories. Cases cover absolute/relative/leading/adjacent globstars and existing dot/nocase/noglobstar contracts. Reference package.json change adds only snap test script; production matching change is minimatch.js. Preflight amendment before inference: exclude the separate hidden-directory makeRe bug (both historical base and reference match it); native basic tests omit exact RegExp rendering snapshots through an in-memory public-source loader, retaining actual matching assertions and the rest of the file. tasks.title: Escaped newlines break arguments in version 9
tasks.contractNotes: Template line continuations must not lose argument characters; verify whitespace, joined words, repeated continuations, interpolation and ordinary compatibility. Cases independently authored from issue plus public template API.

tasks.title: Fix using both `stdin: 'inherit'` and `input` options
tasks.publicBody:
See #1218.

When using any of the following options:
  - `{input: 'foo', stdio: 'inherit'}`   
  - `{input: 'foo', stdio: ['inherit', ...]}`
  - `{input: 'foo', stdin: 'inherit'}`

Execa should silently use the following instead: `{input: 'foo', stdin: 'pipe', ...}`.

Please note that if users need multiple inputs, they can still use the `{stdin: ['inherit', {string: 'foo'}]` option.

This is technically a breaking change, so should be in a major release.
tasks.contractNotes: Explicit input takes precedence over a lone inherited stdin across async/sync and stdin/stdio spellings. Compare two payloads against deliberately different inherited stdin. No external commands or network. Public issue explicitly requests semantic change for major release.

tasks.title: Default value for priority doesn't get applied
tasks.contractNotes: Undefined priority defaults to zero; equal priorities preserve insertion order, explicit priorities sort descending, sizeBy zero sees default-priority items. Native selection tests existing priority cases.

tasks.title: Can't match cursorSave and cursorRestore
tasks.publicBody:
Today I was working with the regex and noticed that [`cursorSave`](https://github.com/sindresorhus/ansi-escapes/blob/main/index.js#L49) and [`cursorRestore` ](https://github.com/sindresorhus/ansi-escapes/blob/main/index.js#L50) don't get stripped with `strip-ansi`.

I didn't check the other use cases yet, but wanted to make sure first that it is correct what I assume here.

It is the case, happy to send a PR.
tasks.contractNotes: Cursor save and restore escape sequences must match completely without consuming adjacent text. Exercise ESC s/u and CSI s/u, default global behavior and onlyFirst; retain SGR/plain-text behavior. Public original issue references ansi-escapes; fix PR #45 explicitly closes #36. Upstream test fixtures and the dev-only ansi-escapes package addition are not production patch paths.

tasks.title: Unable to match links ended with `\u001B` rather than `\u0007`.
tasks.publicBody:
`ansi-regex` cannot match link regexes that end in `\u0001B`, as the regex only allows `\u0007`.

Example: `\x1b]8;;http://example.com/\x1b\\This is a link\x1b]8;;\x1b\\ hello`
Reference: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/53697
tasks.contractNotes: OSC8 hyperlink metadata must be matched through valid ST terminators, preserving the visible caption and neighboring text. Cover ESC-backslash (original reproduction), BEL compatibility, and C1 ST as the equivalent documented ANSI string terminator; include parameterized URI metadata and onlyFirst. Fix PR #58 is explicitly linked as closing #56.

tasks.title: TypeError when string contains certain Unicode Format characters
tasks.contractNotes: Original issue enumerates non-default-ignorable Unicode Format characters and expects zero columns without throwing. Grader checks all 13 listed scalars, mixed visible/format text, Arabic digits and existing plain/CJK/ANSI behaviors. The original issue body includes suggested solutions; retain it exactly as public task input, without adding later solution comments. Requires modern Node with Unicode v regexp support (use Node24).

tasks.title: Negation doesn't work properly with matchBase
tasks.contractNotes: Negated basename patterns must test the basename, with both matchBase and basename aliases; preserve positive, globstar and default non-basename behavior.

tasks.title: basename: true and unixify: true breaks .not()
tasks.publicBody:
_(Thanks for reporting an issue to micromatch! If you haven't already read the [contributor guidelines](contributing.md), Please do that now, then procede to fill out the details below.)_

## Please describe the **minimum necessary steps** to reproduce this issue:

``` shell
$ node
> let mm = require("micromatch")
undefined
> mm.not(["C:\\bla\\bar.xml"], ["*.xml"], {basename: true, unixify: true})
[ 'C:\\bla\\bar.xml' ]
> mm.not(["C:\\bla\\bar.xml"], ["*.xml"], {basename: true, unixify: false})
[]
> mm.not(["C:\\bla\\bar.xml"], ["**/*.xml"], {basename: false, unixify: true})
[ 'C:\\bla\\bar.xml' ]
> mm.not(["C:\\bla\\bar.xml"], ["**/*.xml"], {basename: false, unixify: false})
[]
>
```
…

## What is happening (but shouldn't):

Specifying basename: true and unixify: true  on Windows breaks the .not() function (inverts its logic)

…

## What should be happening instead?

Specifying basename: true and unixify: true  on Windows does not break the .not() function (inverts its logic)

…
tasks.contractNotes: Explicit unixify:true exercises Windows-style strings portably on Linux. .not returns normalized nonmatches, supports basename aliases, multiple patterns and nodupes without mutating caller arrays.

tasks.title: The pattern in the subdirectory gitignore is not correctly excluded
tasks.publicBody:
file structure:
```
.
├── dir
│   ├── .gitignore
│   ├── bar.log
│   └── subdir
│       └── baz.log
└── foo.log
```

`./dir/.gitignore`:
```
*.log
```

List of files to be excluded by git:

```console
$ git check-ignore ./foo.log ./dir/bar.log ./dir/subdir/baz.log
./dir/bar.log
./dir/subdir/baz.log
```

If globby works correctly, only the `foo.log` file should be output:

```js
const globby = require('globby');

(async () => {
  const paths = await globby(['**/*.log'], { gitignore: true });
  console.log(paths);
  // expected: [ 'foo.log' ]
})();
```

However, `globby@11.0.1` outputs like this:

```js
[ 'foo.log', 'dir/subdir/baz.log' ]
```

The file `dir/subdir/baz.log` is not excluded!

---

When `globby@11.0.1` parses the `.gitignore` in a subdirectory, it adds the path of the parent to the beginning of each rule:

https://github.com/sindresorhus/globby/blob/v11.0.1/gitignore.js#L18-L24

So, internally, `globby@11.0.1` has changed the contents of the `./dir/.gitignore` file to look like this:

```diff
- *.log
+ dir/*.log
```

Therefore, you can avoid this problem by modifying the contents of the `./dir/.gitignore` file as follows:

```
**/*.log
```

However, this writing style is redundant. [Most projects will probably be written in the `*.log` style](https://github.com/github/gitignore/blob/18aa6d83774d514da479d73a4beb864cd4220231/Node.gitignore#L3).

I believe this is a bug that should be fixed.
tasks.contractNotes: Nested ignore patterns without middle/leading slash apply below their directory; root scope, slash anchoring, nested path patterns and negation preserve public gitignore semantics. Async, sync and streaming APIs must agree.
